newsitem.title: CHINA: China slams U.S. Congress over Taiwan U.N. bid.
newsitem.headline: China slams U.S. Congress over Taiwan U.N. bid.

text.p: China on Thursday attacked a motion by the U.S. Congress to back a bid by Taiwan to rejoin the United Nations, saying the move would disrupt Sino-U.S. relations.

"The move by the U.S. Congress to go against the flow of history by attempting to split China and disrupt Sino-U.S. relations violates the common will of the international community and will not succeed," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing.
The U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday approved a non-binding resolution supporting Taiwan's efforts to rejoin the United Nations.
Shen said Beijing was seriously concerned and firmly opposed to the U.S. House motion.
"This is gross interference in China's internal affairs and territorial sovereignty," Shen said. "We express our grave concern and firm opposition to this."
Taipei lost its U.N. seat to its arch-rival Beijing in 1972.
The United States ended its official recognition of Taiwan when it established diplomatic ties with Beijing two decades ago, but maintains unofficial ties with the island.
Beijing has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949 and has moved to block the island's attempts to gain greater international recognition.

Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, after meeting with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher in New York on Wednesday, said ties with Washington had improved but that problems still remained on the Taiwan issue.
